item.title: Tanker collides with New Orleans river cruise carrying 129 passengers, rescue operation underway
item.description: A tanker struck and partially submerged a New Orleans river cruise carrying around 129 passengers. Multiple people were rescued as search-and-rescue operations continued.

item.title: EU leaders bring Italy and Poland into Ukraine peace talks team as Kallas fights for spot
item.description: Europe has decided on a joint team for the peace talks led by France, Germany, the UK, Italy, Poland, the EU institutions and NATO. Despite mounting pressure, leaders declined to appoint a single envoy.

item.title: Russia sends major business delegation to Kabul for business talks with the Taliban
item.description: A Russian deputy prime minister led a 70-strong Russian delegation to Afghanistan, pursuing deals on transport, logistics, agriculture, and health products with the Taliban.

item.title: France and Germany near deal on De Cos for ECB top job as EU confirms two candidates
item.description: Two candidates are vying to succeed Christine Lagarde at the ECB, an EU official stated on Friday as EU leaders met in Dublin, while reports coming out of Spain said France and Germany are close to a deal on the central bank's top jobs with Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos as favourite for president.

item.title: Iran MPs debate possible shift in nuclear doctrine and exit from NPT
item.description: Although the US midterm elections result appears to have reduced for now the prospect of a new full-scale US and Israeli attack on Iran, the fundamental US objective of stopping any Iranian nuclear programme is generating an intense debate in the Iranian society and its power circles.

item.title: Berlin clan boss Issa Remmo appears as 'state guest' at EU Parliament event
item.description: The head of the so-called Remmo clan in Berlin, Issa Remo, has officially joined a conference against Islamism in the European Parliament. This is fuelling debate in Germany and Brussels, and many are asking how this is possible.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 13th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 13th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: More live news, more conversations, more Europe: Euronews reinvents itself for its new season
item.description:
Euronews launches its new season on 16 November with more live journalism, new weeknight programmes and a brand-new studio. Its journalists and editorial expertise take centre stage, with more perspectives and deeper insight into the stories shaping Europe.
More Europe than ever, in 12 languages.

item.title: Close-up Photographer of the Year 2026 unveils shortlist of extraordinary nature images
item.description: From extreme close-up portraits of dragonflies to otherworldly mushrooms and some rather creepy crawlers, this year's shortlist offers a fascinating perspective into the hidden minuscule details of our world.

item.title: Azerbaijan intensifies its European engagement at the EPC Summit
item.description: Azerbaijan added additional thrust to its engagement with Europe announcing more energy to the EU, a strategic partnership with the UK, additional agreements with Ukraine, a dozen bilateral meetings with European leaders and a new meeting with Armenia to advance the historic peace process.

item.title: UK: Christmas at Kew 2026 unveils spectacular light trail in London
item.description: London's Kew Gardens has unveiled a dazzling Christmas light trail featuring more than a million lights and 24 installations. A spectacular new fountain and laser show takes centre stage.

item.title: EU leaders discuss how to boost Europe's AI industry while tackling risks at Dublin summit
item.description: European leaders together with Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch and AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton discussed how Europe can build its AI industry while making sure the technology is developed responsibly.

item.title: Kallas says 'Russians don't want me' as EU envoy for peace talks
item.description: Kaja Kallas has made a strong push to be appointed special EU envoy for the peace negotiations. But "Russians do not want me", she added.

item.title: North Macedonia: Kriva Palanka seeks help over 1,000 free-roaming cows
item.description: More than 1,000 cows are roaming freely through Kriva Palanka in North Macedonia, damaging property and alarming residents. The mayor wants the government to declare a 30-day state of crisis.

item.title: The right to a home: Spain’s cooperative answer to the housing crisis
item.description: As Spain faces a deepening housing crisis, a Barcelona-based cooperative offers an alternative to renting and buying. Its non-profit, right-to-use model provides affordable, long-term homes. Could it help tackle Europe's housing crisis?

item.title: Nvidia has lost nearly $2tn in value. What could it be worth without Jensen Huang?
item.description: Nvidia has lost about $1.8tn (€1.6tn) in market value since its record close on 6 October. After Jensen Huang’s exit, investors are weighing whether the chipmaker can keep growing at the pace that made it the biggest name in AI.

item.title: China warns US over chip curbs as suspected spy’s firm got banned chips
item.description: The row threatens to overshadow next week’s expected Trump-Xi meeting, as Congress pushes for tougher limits on sales to Beijing.

item.title: Turkey: Six-metre Trojan Horse spills plastic waste at COP31
item.description: A giant Trojan Horse overflowing with plastic waste has appeared in Antalya as Greenpeace International staged a striking environmental protest during the COP31 climate summit. Created with Danish artist Thomas Dambo, the Greenpeace installation warns of the environmental impact of plastics.

item.title: Microsoft 365 global outage disrupts Portuguese government, health services and schools
item.description: A global failure in Microsoft services is disrupting several sectors in Portugal. The outage since Thursday affects Outlook and Teams, though the company reports progress in restoring access.

item.title: Rosalía's 'Lux' dominates Latin Grammys as Argentine artists shine
item.description: The Catalan artist wins five of seven awards, including song and album of the year. Milo J's folk tribute triumphs, with 'Niño' best recording and nine more prizes for Argentines.

item.title: From Ukraine peace to Europe's future: How Russia is shifting the debate
item.description: As talks to end Russia’s war in Ukraine make little progress, Moscow is pushing for a wider deal on Europe’s security, raising fears that the Kremlin is seeking to reshape the continent’s future on its own terms.

item.title: Hungary’s MOL seeks EU funding as CEO warns Russian oil phase-out could trigger social unrest
item.description: MOL says it could phase out Russian oil imports by the end of 2027, but chief Bacsa warns that higher energy costs could fuel political instability in Hungary and Slovakia. He is calling for EU funding to expand alternative pipeline routes, as Brussels keeps focus on quitting Russian energy.

item.title: At least three killed and more than 20 injured in Russian strikes on Ukraine
item.description: It comes as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrapped up a meeting with US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Ireland on Thursday.

item.title: 'Take your time': Funniest reactions to Microsoft global outage
item.description: The outage has been reported in more than 70 countries and is impacting millions of users globally. Still, that hasn't stopped the internet from having a laugh...

item.title: Winter 2026 travel tips: The best dates to fly and book hotels
item.description: Expedia's latest winter travel outlook report reveals the cheapest and most expensive dates to fly and book accommodation, when airports will be busiest and which destinations are seeing the biggest rise in demand.

item.title: European diesel prices stay high as global oil supply overtakes demand, IEA says
item.description: European diesel prices are still 77% above pre-war levels, the IEA said on Friday. Global oil supplies are expected to exceed demand in the fourth quarter as Gulf exports recover.

item.title: China to encourage investment in Turkish renewable energy with $15bn solar and wind deal
item.description: Türkiye wants to sharply expand solar and wind power by 2040 and is seeking foreign investment to fund the work.

item.title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'Club Kid' - Sex, drugs & sudden parenthood
item.description: A gay party promoter is suddenly faced with fatherhood in a familiar but engaging debut from Jordan Firstman, who ensures you'll be charmed and (nearly) moved to tears.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 13th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 13th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Huang and US Commerce Secretary Lutnick summoned to testify before Congress
item.description: Huang's decision to exit Nvidia 33 years after founding the company came as reports emerged that he had had a relationship with an executive at the firm. He had already been facing scrutiny over reports of an affair with an alleged spy.

item.title: How a new ‘green energy corridor’ from the Caspian Sea could help Eastern Europe kick fossil fuels
item.description: The partnership signed at the COP31 climate summit aims to transform Azerbaijan into an interregional electricity hub.

item.title: Darth Vader's lightsaber breaks Star Wars auction record by selling for nearly €4.5 million
item.description: Auctioneers estimated the on screen prop would sell for over $1m, but the lightsaber used by Darth Vader in the famous “I am your father” scene ended up selling for nearly $5m.

item.title: Ukraine: Russian drone attacks hit Kyiv hospital, leave two dead in Odesa
item.description: Russian overnight attacks on Ukraine killed at least two person in Odesa and injured another at a hospital in Kyiv. Rescuers evacuated patients, including people using wheelchairs and crutches, as firefighters battled the flames.

item.title: ExxonMobil sues EU over rules forcing oil giants to invest in carbon storage
item.description: US oil giant ExxonMobil is challenging EU rules requiring fossil fuel producers to help fund carbon storage infrastructure, in a legal battle that could undermine Brussels’ efforts to make the industry pay for the energy transition.

item.title: Why the UK wants to jail undersea cable saboteurs and why tougher punishment may not be enough
item.description: The United Kingdom is seeking tougher penalties for damaging critical underwater infrastructure, but industry insiders warn that stronger rules alone cannot prevent widespread disruption.

item.title: Microsoft outage explained: what went wrong and is your data at risk?
item.description: Governments, doctor surgeries and even rival AI firms have been caught up, and the episode is sharpening questions about Europe's reliance on a handful of US tech giants.

item.title: Dementia risk increases with number of cigarettes smoked per day
item.description: Researchers found that dementia risk increases with the number of cigarettes smoked per day, rising by 16% for those who smoke 10 a day and by 34% for those who smoke 20, compared with people who have never smoked.

item.title: US denies IRGC destroyed American radar in Bahrain after attack on southern Iran
item.description: Despite rising military tensions, diplomatic efforts mediated by Qatar and Pakistan are continuing. Tehran has made any resumption of formal negotiations with Washington conditional on its demands being met.

item.title: José Pinhal's rediscovered songs sell out Porto and Lisbon Coliseums
item.description: A tribute band to an artist who was only known in an ultra-restricted circle while alive sent the Coliseu dos Recreios wild at its farewell concert. Understanding the José Pinhal phenomenon means grasping our century's drive to reclaim nuggets from the past.

item.title: Swedish pop sensation Robyn brands Eurovision ‘embarrassing’
item.description: Swedish pop star Robyn, whose hits include 'With Every Heartbeat' and 'Dancing On My Own', shared her verdict on Eurovision during an appearance on Amy Poehler's podcast. She suggested Eurovision's appeal had diminished for her since ABBA’s involvement, and that it was "embarrassing".

item.title: Portugal: Humanoid robots take centre stage at Web Summit 2026
item.description: Dancing humanoid robots and robotic dogs stole the show at Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon. The technology conference has generated nearly €2.5 billion for Portugal's economy over the past decade, according to a study.

item.title: Outlook outage: how to keep working and which email alternatives you can use
item.description: After Microsoft 365 services went down on 12 November, affecting millions of users worldwide, here is how you can keep using Outlook while the issue is fixed.

item.title: Flying Blue flies high: These are the best airline rewards programmes in Europe
item.description: Air France-KLM's Flying Blue was crowned the best frequent flyer scheme globally thanks to how easy it is to earn and spend miles. The British Airways Club and Virgin Atlantic Flying Club also ranked high.

item.title: What is next for Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang resigns?
item.description: The AI chip giant has no leader in waiting, may lose its voice in Washington, and has big bets in Europe that its founder championed in person.

item.title: 'The market will look for alternatives,' on Huang resignation says Andrea Renda, Digital Economy expert
item.description: Nvidia is at the centre of the global artificial intelligence revolution. But the American chip giant is now facing an extraordinary crisis, following the shock resignation of its CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of an espionage scandal.

item.title: 'The structure of the European economy needs to change more quickly,' says IMF Europe chief Mateusz Szczurek
item.description: Europe's economy is facing a dangerous combination of challenges: sluggish growth, mounting public debt and rising borrowing costs. As sovereign bond yields put pressure on government finances, Europe's ability to invest in its future is increasingly in question.

item.title: European shares fall as Nvidia CEO’s exit raises doubts over AI boom
item.description: Equity markets mostly fell on Friday, following losses on Wall Street as investors weighed what Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia could mean for the AI industry. Oil prices rose after US President Donald Trump said Washington did not need a deal with Iran.

item.title: Peru: Pope Leo XIV leads youth prayer vigil at Lima's National Stadium
item.description: Thousands of young Catholics gathered at Peru's National Stadium in Lima on Thursday 12 November for a prayer vigil led by Pope Leo XIV, transforming the venue into a sea of lights, The stands lit up with thousands of mobile phone lights as the pontiff led an evening of songs, prayer and reflection.

item.title: Cause and effect: American rebels through the eyes of Jean-Pierre Laffont
item.description: New York in the 1960s, like much of the United States, is unrecognisable from the land many of us know today. French photographer Jean-Pierre Laffont captured all manner of daily life in the city, and beyond, in a stunning new book, "Rebels with a Cause".

item.title: US pushes for European presence at Ukraine-Russia talks, which Moscow refuses to confirm
item.description: "Both sides have now agreed to expand the next round of negotiations to include our European partners," US special envoy Jared Kushner said. Moscow has not confirmed whether it has agreed to include European negotiators in subsequent talks.
